Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
The `parse` method in the `ComplexFormat` class is responsible for parsing a string to create a `Complex` object. The method involves parsing real and imaginary parts of the complex number along with handling signs and whitespace.

Looking at the code snippet of the `parse` method, the failure reported in the current bug report (`java.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`) occurs at line 374 of the `ComplexFormat` class. This line tries to parse the imaginary character from the input string `source` by comparing a substring of `source` with the configured imaginary character. If the comparison fails, the method returns null and sets the error index.

The issue reported in the current bug report indicates that the method does not check whether the imaginary character is set or not before trying to parse it. This leads to a situation where the method can attempt to access characters beyond the length of the `source` string, causing the `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`.

To resolve this issue, the `parse` method should include a check to ensure that there are enough characters in the `source` string before attempting to parse the imaginary character.

Next, I will identify the method that needs to be fixed to address this issue.
